gross_visual_qc.reviewer: Codex visual inspection; not radiologist review
gross_visual_qc.labels: Opaque subject IDs and fixed slice fractions; no diagnosis or model outcome displayed
findings: Every available subject has a recognizable inferior-to-superior axial anatomical sequence; no blank or corrupted rendered image was observed.
Head pitch, cranial shape, relative anatomical levels, image sharpness and intensity vary. Fractions do not provide atlas-aligned anatomy.
Anterior extracranial cutouts and peripheral tissue appearance vary across subjects; source preprocessing and image appearance remain possible confounders.
No gross brain truncation attributable to the square display crop was apparent at montage scale.
All29available subjects are retained. The30thparticipant has no provider T1 and remains explicitly listed as unavailable.
gross_visual_qc.scope: Gross rendering/anatomical plausibility only, not diagnostic review, validated segmentation/localization, defacing certification, or clinical image-quality adjudication.

limitations: Gross rendering QC does not establish clinical or anatomical validity.
The original fixed heuristic has no atlas registration, validated skull stripping, bias-field correction, or scanner harmonization.
Exact duplicate checks do not establish patient independence against unidentified legacy source data.
A small single-site probable-AD/healthy-control cohort cannot establish real-world clinical readiness.
Missing T1 is retained and reported; no replacement or imputation is performed.
